records.How to use: Use the full-access button to browse the therapeutic areas and company pages. Review the methodology and trial-level factors behind every approval estimate. Track readouts and protocol dates separately from actual published results.
records.Free scope: The operator says all 13 therapeutic areas, trial pages, exports, newsletter, reports, and features are open in the current beta with no account or payment. Terms say a future paid service would be announced in advance.
records.Main limitation: The approval likelihood is a provider-calibrated estimate based on published transition rates and selected trial factors. Exact adjustment weights are not published. Historical evaluation covers trials that started 2012 to 2016 and does not establish future predictive accuracy.
records.Caution: ClinicalTrials.gov contains sponsor-reported registry data and can lag trial events. Estimated completion dates are not readout dates. A probability estimate is not a forecast of company share performance or a substitute for reading trial results.
records.Source check: Provider trial dashboard, open-access terms, data sources, and methodology reviewed
records.Account: No account or payment in current beta
records.Freshness note: The dashboard page reviewed October 12, 2026 said the data were current through October 11, covered 28,485 active trials, and included all 13 therapeutic areas. The provider says it refreshes weekly.

records.Name: SupplierFinder US Import Statistics Explorer
records.Theme: Monthly import values and trade lanes by country, HS code, and port
records.Geography: United States imports, 230 partner countries, 217 US ports
records.Access: Free unlimited search and CSV export; no account
records.Observable signal: Official US import value, weight, transport mode, and calculated duties by reporting country, HS code, port, and monthly period, with trends and CSV export.
records.Research use: Check monthly import mix and origin or port changes for semiconductor, hardware, industrial, and consumer product categories. Use it for aggregate supply-chain context rather than supplier-level company demand.
records.How to use: Search a country, HS code, or US port, confirm the HS definition, compare monthly values and weight, and export the table. Separate nominal value shifts from physical-volume shifts and verify material categories against the official source.
records.Free scope: The provider says search, all displayed data, and CSV exports are free without registration, account, or usage limits. It says there is no paid tier restricting the visible dataset.
records.Main limitation: The tool contains aggregate customs statistics rather than named buyers, suppliers, bills of lading, or company-specific imports. The latest data shown during this review were for July 2026.
records.Caution: HS categories can include different products and parts. Import value, weight, port of entry, and origin country do not identify final demand, inventory, or any single issuer’s shipments.
records.Source check: Provider search page, dated update labels, FAQ, and monthly country table reviewed
records.Freshness note: The provider page and FAQ reviewed October 12, 2026 said its latest data were updated through July 2026. A public country page displayed monthly import tables and CSV exports; the monthly tool cites official US government trade statistics.

records.Name: Dublin City Centre Pedestrian Footfall
records.Access: Free hourly counter downloads under CC BY
records.Observable signal: Hourly passersby at fixed city-centre pedestrian counter locations
records.Research use: Track high-street activity at hourly and seasonal frequency, then compare with nearby retail and dining performance
records.How to use: Download the latest CSV or XLSX and the counter-location file. Match counters to nearby stores and compare equivalent hours, weekdays and seasonal periods.
records.Free scope: Public hourly count files and counter coordinates are downloadable without an account. Dataset metadata lists a Creative Commons Attribution license.
records.Main limitation: Counts people passing fixed outdoor sensors, not store entries, purchases or chainwide traffic. Recent resource currently runs through September 2, 2026, so it is not live.
records.Caution: Treat a nearby counter as a corridor-level proxy. Sensor outages and location changes can affect the series. Attribute Dublin City Council and the NTA.
records.Source check: Official dataset and downloadable resource list reviewed
records.Freshness note: Dataset metadata says monthly updates. Latest listed file reviewed October 12 covers January 1 through September 2, 2026; this is a delayed file release, not a real-time feed.

records.Name: Leicester Pedestrian Flow Data
records.Access: Free quarterly count files and dashboard
records.Observable signal: Quarterly average pedestrian volume at selected city sites
records.Research use: Monitor direction of local town-centre footfall and compare it with nearby retailers or hospitality venues
records.How to use: Open the city dashboard or download the quarterly XLSX/CSV. Compare like-for-like sites and quarters. Check the notes for sensor gaps before using a change.
records.Free scope: Public spreadsheet and machine-readable files are downloadable through data.gov.uk without an account. The dataset page states the Open Government Licence applies unless otherwise noted, but this specific dataset does not list a separate licence.
records.Main limitation: Selected sensor points only, not citywide or store-entry counts. Daily averages are per quarter and missing sensor periods can be filled with historical averages.
records.Caution: A nearby pedestrian counter can be a local activity proxy, not a proxy for a retailer’s conversion or sales.
records.Source check: Official dataset page, date, export links and limitations reviewed
records.Freshness note: Dataset page last updated June 17, 2026; a quarterly file was available on review. Use the dated file, not the quarterly cadence claim, as the freshness reference.

records.Name: Downtown Seattle Monthly Foot-Traffic Dashboard
records.Geography: Downtown Seattle, including Pike Place Market
records.Observable signal: Monthly unique visitors, total visits, worker activity, Pike Place Market visitation and selected spending indicators versus 2019
records.Research use: Track downtown Seattle visitation and tourism as contextual demand evidence for local retail, restaurants and urban-core property exposure
records.How to use: Read the monthly dashboard and compare the same period with 2019 and the prior year. Use the notes to distinguish unique visitors from visits and visitor traffic from workers. Check the data-provider label for each metric.
records.Free scope: The Downtown Seattle Association publishes its dashboard and charts publicly without an account. It asks users to credit the association when reusing charts, data or images.
records.Main limitation: Geography is downtown Seattle, not an individual retailer or a national panel. Foot-traffic data come from Placer.ai, count each person once per day and exclude international visitors. Monthly visitor totals are not same-store sales.
records.Caution: Dashboard commentary can mix observation periods across indicators. As of this review visitor counts were August 2026 while the spending number was July 2026. Attribute the association and respect its chart/data reuse request.
records.Source check: Public dashboard and source notes reviewed
records.Freshness note: September 2026 dashboard contains August 2026 visitor data. It reports nearly 3.8 million unique visitors, 112% of August 2019, and 9.2 million visits. Spending cited is July data. Foot traffic is sourced from Placer.ai.
